title: XPROC-NEURAL Network Optimization — Fix Bugs, Wire Closed-Loop, Ingest Real Data, Modernize Architecture
brief: Address the systemic gaps surfaced by the 5-way (3 Claude + Codex + Gemini-fallback) assessment of 2026-05-07. The XPROC-NEURAL stack has 47 engines on disk but: (a) two correctness bugs in T1-02 (W2 backprop update-order, response_summary.success label leakage), (b) 42 of 47 engines have ZERO production callers, (c) FeedbackBusEngine (P0-U04 promise) was never built, (d) 24,545 JM Die NC programs unutilized, (e) 32→16→3 MLP is 2015-era vs CatBoost/FT-Transformer SOTA, (f) tier composition exists in code but not at runtime. This roadmap closes those gaps in priority order: correctness first, then closed-loop wiring, then real data, then architecture modernization, then tier composition.

phases.title: Phase 1 — T1-02 Correctness Fixes (BLOCKS EVERYTHING ELSE)
phases.rationale: Codex Reviewer #4 found two correctness bugs that invalidate every training run. Both are trivial fixes (~10 lines each) but every downstream phase assumes a correct learner. Fix these first.

units.title: Fix W2 update-order backprop bug — snapshot W2 before in-place update
exit_conditions: Snapshot W2 into local Float64Array BEFORE the W2/b2 momentum updates at line 647-656
dHiddenPre at line 660-667 reads from snapshot, not this.W2
Existing test CrossProcessNeuralLearningEngine.test.ts still passes (mathematical equivalence preserved for FORWARD pass; gradient direction now correct)
Add new test case asserting that for a fixed (x, y) input, dW1[h,i] equals (numeric-gradient-at-x via finite-difference) within 1e-4 tolerance — proves backprop math correct
abort_criteria: Snapshot allocation in stepOne measurably slows per-step time (>20% regression)
Existing 363 session-touched tests fail
Numeric-gradient check fails after fix
units.description: Codex review finding (line 647-664): the inner loop updates W2 in-place at lines 647-656, then computes dHiddenPre at line 660-667 using this.W2 — but that's the POST-UPDATE W2, not the forward-pass W2. Standard fix: copy W2 into a local Float64Array of size [OUTPUT_DIM × HIDDEN_DIM] before the W2 update loop, then use the snapshot in dHiddenPre computation. Cost: ~16 floats × ~3 multiplies per step. Must add a finite-difference numeric-gradient test that proves the fix produces the mathematically correct gradient.

units.title: Remove response_summary.success label leakage at line 314
exit_conditions: featurize() no longer reads response_summary.success
Confirm via grep: zero remaining references to record.response_summary?.success in featurize
Re-run NeuralLearningE2EConvergence.test.ts: train accuracy may drop (acceptable if drop < 15% — proves the leak was real signal)
Document drop magnitude in commit message
Add regression test: synthesize records where response_summary.success is RANDOMLY set independent of outcome.kind; assert train accuracy doesn't move materially (proves no leak)
abort_criteria: Train accuracy drops below 0.45 (worse than random + 10% margin) on the synthetic dataset
Random-success-flag regression test shows accuracy IS affected (means leakage path still exists)
units.description: Reviewers 3 and 4 independently flagged: featurize() at line 314 injects response_summary.success (-1/0/+1) into the input vector. response_summary.success is downstream of outcome.kind in the data model (it's set BY the outcome). This means the model can shortcut-learn: if response_summary.success is True, predict outcome=success. Remove this feature. Expect train accuracy to drop on the current synthetic dataset (which sets both fields consistently).

units.title: Honest finalLoss reporting — recompute post-update on full epoch
exit_conditions: TrainResult.finalLoss is computed via computeMeanLoss() AFTER the last epoch's updates, not accumulated mid-update
TrainResult adds initialLoss field that uses the same forward-only computation BEFORE any updates
E2E convergence test asserts finalLoss < initialLoss * 0.7 still holds with the new HONEST measurement
Document the methodological change in JSDoc: 'finalLoss is post-training mean cross-entropy on the training set with updated weights'
abort_criteria: Honest finalLoss measurement reveals the model was NOT actually converging — convergence test fails
Per-epoch loss curve becomes non-monotonic (oscillating)
units.description: Codex finding: lines 376-387 accumulate per-sample losses computed BEFORE each sample's update. The 'finalLoss' is therefore a moving target, not a converged measurement. Use computeMeanLoss(samples) AFTER the last epoch with frozen weights for finalLoss, AND BEFORE the first epoch for initialLoss. This makes the convergence claim mathematically defensible.

units.title: True minibatch SGD with gradient averaging
exit_conditions: stepOne replaced with stepBatch(x[], y[]) that accumulates gradients across the batch then applies a single weight update with mean(grads)
Per-sample stepOne kept as a private helper for online-update path
Existing E2E convergence test passes with batch_size=16 — model still learns
Add test: with batch_size=1 and batch_size=N (full batch), trained weights are different and both converge to similar accuracy
Document in JSDoc that batch_size now means TRUE minibatch (gradients averaged), not 'sample-by-sample within a batch boundary'
abort_criteria: True minibatch convergence is materially slower than current online-SGD on synthetic data (>2x epochs needed)
Test count drops below 363 session-touched
units.description: Codex #4 finding: current code loops sample-by-sample with per-sample updates inside batch boundaries — that's online SGD with arbitrary periodicity, not minibatch SGD. Hyperparameter 'batch_size' is misleading. Implement proper batch gradient accumulation: accumulate dLogits, dHiddenPre, etc. across batch_size samples, then apply ONE update with the averaged gradients.

units.title: Statistical convergence test — ln(3) baseline + repeated-seed CI
exit_conditions: New test case: train across 5 different seeds, assert mean(finalAcc) > random + 2*std-error (statistically significant beat over chance)
New test case: assert initialLoss is within ±0.15 of ln(3)≈1.099 (random softmax baseline)
New test case: assert finalLoss reduction is statistically distinguishable from a no-op (5-seed mean test)
Test runtime stays below 30 seconds (acceptable for CI)
abort_criteria: Repeated-seed mean accuracy fails to clear chance + 2σ at 5 seeds
Test runtime exceeds 60 seconds
units.description: Codex finding: 'loss reduces ≥30%' is not statistically significant — what's the variance across seeds? This unit adds the missing statistical rigor. Run 5 seeds, compute mean ± std-error of accuracy, assert mean > 1/3 + 2*SE. Also assert initialLoss matches the theoretical ln(3) for a 3-class softmax with random weights.

criteria: U-NN-FIX01..05 all status:completed
All 363 session-touched tests still pass
New finite-difference numeric-gradient test passes (proves U-NN-FIX01 correct)
Random-success-flag regression test passes (proves U-NN-FIX02 closed the leak)
5-seed CI test passes (proves U-NN-FIX03 + U-NN-FIX05 statistically valid)

phases.title: Phase 2 — Featurization Upgrade (categorical buckets, normalization, RAG, physics features)
phases.rationale: Reviewer 3 identified that 4-bucket categorical hash → ~76% collision rate for 8 materials. Reviewer 1 identified that the wiki tribal tips, physics engines, and existing CrossDisciplinaryDeepLearningEngine outputs are never fed as features. Featurization is the bottleneck.

units.title: Widen categorical hash buckets — material 4→64, tool/machine/op 3→16, with collision audit
exit_conditions: MATERIAL_BUCKETS = 64; TOOL_MATERIAL_BUCKETS = 16; MACHINE_FAMILY_BUCKETS = 16; OPERATION_BUCKETS = 16
INPUT_DIM recomputed and asserted in test (was 32, now will be ~64+ — adjust HIDDEN_DIM if necessary or use a projection)
Add collision-audit test: feed 100 distinct material strings (read from H:/prism/mcp-server/src/data/materials/), assert collision rate < 5%
E2E convergence test still passes
Persist bucket counts in serialize()/loadFrom() so loaded models bind to the same featurization
abort_criteria: INPUT_DIM expansion forces HIDDEN_DIM doubling that pushes param count > 5000 (overfit risk on small data)
Collision audit shows < 5% collisions but train accuracy DROPS post-fix (suggests the hash is hashing to fewer effective buckets than nominal)
units.description: Reviewers 3 and 4 both flagged the catastrophically narrow hash buckets. Material has only 4 buckets vs 100+ real materials in the corpus → ~76% collision rate. Widen and add audit.

units.title: Welford z-score normalization for numeric features
exit_conditions: Add running mean/var via Welford's online algorithm, persisted in SerializedNeural
featurize() applies (x - mean) / sqrt(var + eps) per numeric feature
Replace LOG1P_NUMERIC_DIVISOR magic constant entirely (it's a one-size-fits-all scaling that obscures real distributions)
First N=30 samples bypass normalization (warmup), use raw values clipped to [-3, +3]
Add test: train with widely different numeric scales (RPM 100 vs 30000), confirm convergence is NOT scale-sensitive after normalization
Adam (P5) will need this — z-scoring is a precondition for stable adaptive optimizers
abort_criteria: Welford state corruption across save/load roundtrip (mean/var diverge)
Per-step time regression > 15% from added normalization
units.description: Reviewer 3 finding: log1p(v)/12 is one-size-fits-all. Numeric features span RPM (100-30000) vs target_ra_um (0.4-12) vs depth_of_cut_mm (0.1-5). Need per-feature normalization.

units.title: Physics-engine features — Kienzle force, Taylor life, chatter stability appended to input
exit_conditions: PhysicsFeatureExtractorEngine.extract(record) returns Float64Array of physics-derived features
Features include (z-scored): predicted_kienzle_force_N, predicted_taylor_life_min, predicted_chatter_stability_lobe_index, predicted_surface_ra_um, predicted_thermal_load_W
T1-02 input grows by 5 features (with corresponding hidden-layer adjustment)
Test: with physics features, T1-02 reaches higher accuracy on synthetic dataset than without (or document why not)
Engine wired into prism_intelligence dispatcher as xproc_physics_features action
Symmetry test (XprocDispatcherSymmetry) updated and still passes
abort_criteria: Physics engines (Kienzle/Taylor/Chatter) throw on edge-case inputs (missing tool material, zero RPM) — must handle gracefully
Physics features add training time > 50% (Kienzle is fast but composition is slow)
units.description: Reviewer 1 finding: existing physics engines never feed the NN. Build a feature extractor that calls the existing engines (do NOT inline physics constants — import from src/physics/constants.ts). Wires the entire physics-engine library to provide features. This is the T8 (Neuro-Symbolic) vision activated for input, not just output gating.

units.title: Wiki tribal-tip RAG features via PRISMSelfAwarenessEngine
exit_conditions: WikiRAGFeatureEngine.extractRAGFeatures(record) calls prismSelfAwarenessEngine.searchTribalKnowledge(material+operation), returns top-5 tip count + average rule-firing intensity as 8 features
Cache RAG queries (LRU, max 1000 entries) to avoid wiki re-search on every record
Confirm via grep: WikiRAGFeatureEngine is referenced from CrossProcessNeuralLearningEngine.featurize()
Train accuracy on the synthetic dataset improves OR documented why not (synthetic dataset may not have wiki coverage)
abort_criteria: PRISMSelfAwarenessEngine.searchTribalKnowledge is itself unwired or returns empty for plausible queries
Per-record RAG query time > 5ms (forces caching to kick in)
units.description: Reviewer 1 finding: zero CrossProcess*Engine.ts references searchTribalKnowledge. Build a RAG feature engine that uses the stable PRISMSelfAwarenessEngine API to convert wiki context into features. 3,700 tips + 296 playbook rules become accessible to the NN.

criteria: Categorical collisions < 5% on real material catalog
z-score normalization preserves train/test parity
Physics features and RAG features both wired and tested
T1-02 input dim > 64 (was 32) — model has materially richer signal

phases.title: Phase 3 — Closed-Loop Wiring (FeedbackBus, P2P emission, NN auto-train, memory feedback)
phases.rationale: Reviewer 2 found 42 of 47 engines have ZERO production callers. The promised FeedbackBusEngine (P0-U04) was never built. No print-to-program engine emits outcome events. This phase wires the missing event flow that makes 'closed-loop learning' real instead of aspirational.

units.title: Build FeedbackBusEngine — pub/sub event bus for outcome events
exit_conditions: FeedbackBusEngine implements subscribe(topic, callback), publish(topic, event), unsubscribe(handle)
In-process EventEmitter backing; no external deps
Subscribers fire async (queueMicrotask) so a slow subscriber doesn't block the publisher
Try/catch around each subscriber invocation — one crashing subscriber doesn't break others (per P0-U04 spec)
≥10 vitest cases: subscribe + publish round-trip; multiple subscribers; subscriber crash isolation; unsubscribe; publish to nonexistent topic; concurrent publish ordering
Wired into prism_intelligence as xproc_feedbackbus_publish / _subscribe / _stats / _topics actions
Symmetry test still passes (action count balanced across both dispatchers)
abort_criteria: Subscriber crash propagates to publisher
Memory leak: unsubscribed handlers retained
units.description: P0-U04 from INFRA-NEURAL-LEDGER-MS1 was never built. Build it now. Reviewer 2 identified this as 'the single missing primitive that converts the 47-node forest into a graph'.

units.title: Wire CrossProcessOutcomeStore to publish on FeedbackBus when records arrive
exit_conditions: OutcomeStore.record() and recordOutcome() publish to FeedbackBus on topic 'outcome.recorded' / 'outcome.finalized'
Publish is fire-and-forget (try/catch, never blocks main path)
Test: subscribe then record N events, assert all events arrived in order with correct topics
abort_criteria: Publishing breaks existing OutcomeStore tests (78 cases)
Publish is synchronous and slows record() by > 5ms
units.description: Connect Tier 1 ledger to the pub/sub bus. Now any subscriber can react to outcome events.

units.title: NeuralLearningEngine subscribes to FeedbackBus for incremental online training
exit_conditions: On import, NeuralLearningEngine.subscribe('outcome.finalized', this.onNewOutcome)
onNewOutcome buffers events; flushes when buffer reaches MIN_BATCH=8 OR every 60 seconds (whichever first)
Flush triggers a single online stepBatch (per U-NN-FIX04)
Subscription handle stored so test isolation engines can unsubscribe
Test: publish 100 outcome events through FeedbackBus, assert NN.totalSamplesSeen increased by 100
abort_criteria: Subscription causes singleton tests to interfere (events from other tests training the singleton)
Online training degrades batch-trained accuracy (catastrophic forgetting)
units.description: Closes the loop: outcome event → bus → NN auto-trains. This is the heartbeat of the closed-loop system.

units.title: Wire MillPrintToProgramEngine to emit outcome events post-run
exit_conditions: After every successful program generation: crossProcessOutcomeStore.record({bridge:'p2p', process:'mill', request_summary, response_summary, outcome:{kind:'pending'}})
Operator-confirmed runs (via separate skill) update the same record's outcome.kind = success/failure/operator_override
Existing MillingPrintToProgramEngine tests still pass
New test: generate a program, assert outcome event emitted to OutcomeStore
Coordinate with peer chat owning MillingPrintToProgramEngine.ts (currently claude-bee98bb8 per chat-bus) — may need to split this unit
abort_criteria: MillingPrintToProgramEngine claimed by another chat at unit start time
Emission adds > 10ms to program generation
units.description: Reviewer 2 finding: zero PrintToProgram engines emit outcome events. Wire the mill side first (most data volume).

units.title: Wire WEDMPrintToProgramEngine to emit outcome events (Reviewer 5 Option A)
exit_conditions: WEDM emission with kerf-width target as primary outcome metric
Wire-break events emit outcome.kind='failure' with failure_mode='wire_break'
Reviewer 5 recommended WEDM as the FIRST closed-loop pilot — this unit ships that pilot
Smoke-test: generate a WEDM program, simulate operator confirmation, assert NN trains on the resulting outcome event
abort_criteria: WEDMPrintToProgramEngine doesn't exist on this branch (verify via Glob)
units.description: Reviewer 5 explicitly recommended WEDM as the MVP closed-loop pilot — most mature, JM Die has the data.

units.title: Memory feedback ingester — feedback_*.md → RewardShaperEngine
exit_conditions: Glob `C:/Users/wompu/.claude/projects/H--prism/memory/feedback_*.md`
Parse each: extract first H1 + tone classifier (Ollama for batch, fallback to keyword heuristic)
Emit reward signal to crossProcessRewardShaperEngine (T4) with sign aligned to operator correction
Wired as scheduled cron (daily) via PRISM cron registry
≥10 test cases: parse representative files, classify tone, verify reward sign, missing-file handling, malformed-frontmatter handling
abort_criteria: Tone classifier hallucinates positive/negative on neutral memos
Reward magnitudes overwhelm shop-floor signal (need normalization to ±1)
units.description: Reviewer 1 finding: memory feedback files never flow to T4 RL. Wire them now. Unblocks an entire dormant tier for free.

criteria: Live demo: simulate WEDM job → outcome event → bus → NN auto-trains → next prediction reflects new data
FeedbackBusEngine 100% test coverage on its public API
Connected-engine count rises from 5/47 to ≥15/47 per Reviewer 2's metric

phases.title: Phase 4 — Real Data Ingestion (24,545 JM Die NC programs → outcome events)
phases.rationale: Reviewer 1 found 24,545 JM Die production NC programs sitting unused. Each shipped program is implicitly a 'success' label by definition. This phase parses them and replays through the NN pipeline — 1000× the current synthetic dataset volume.

units.title: JM Die NC corpus parser — Mastercam-Okuma dialect (lathe priority)
exit_conditions: Parses program header (material, tool table, customer)
Extracts per-tool: SFM, feed/rev, depth-of-cut, operation type
Test against 10 known programs from JM DIE/CNC LATHE/, assert extracted fields match hand-validated truth
Handles malformed/truncated programs without crash
Supports Mastercam-Okuma dialect first (per JM Die machine inventory)
abort_criteria: < 80% of JM Die lathe corpus parses cleanly (need broader dialect support)
units.description: Reviewer 1 documented that JM Die programs have parseable Mastercam/Okuma headers (`STEEL INCH - 1030 - 200 BHN`, `T010101`, `G96 S200`, `F.005`). Build the parser.

units.title: Extend parser — Mastercam-Fanuc + hyperMILL dialects
exit_conditions: Fanuc dialect: handles G54-G59 work offsets, G96/G97 surface speed, G50 spindle clamp
hyperMILL dialect: handles its specific comment header patterns
Coverage rises to ≥95% of JM Die corpus parsing cleanly
abort_criteria: Coverage plateau below 90%
units.description: Multi-dialect support unlocks the full 24,545-file corpus.

units.title: Bulk corpus → outcome events ingester
exit_conditions: Script walks H:/prism/JM DIE/, parses each program, emits outcome event with kind='success' (shipped) by default
Customer-specific overrides (where JM Die metadata indicates rework or scrap) emit kind='operator_override' or kind='failure'
Idempotency: re-running script doesn't duplicate events (de-dup by program_path hash)
Final count: ≥20,000 outcome events ingested
Train-T1-02-on-real-corpus regression test: assert val accuracy > 60% on a held-out 20% (vs 50% on synthetic)
abort_criteria: Ingestion overflows OutcomeStore's 100MB rotation threshold (need archival)
Real-corpus train accuracy is WORSE than synthetic (model overfits to JM Die's idiosyncrasies)
units.rollback_procedure: Truncate OutcomeStore.jsonl back to pre-ingest checkpoint
units.description: The headline data win. 24,545 real programs become the training set. T1-02 stops being trained on synthetic and starts being trained on production.

criteria: ≥20,000 real outcome events in OutcomeStore
T1-02 trained on real corpus, validated calibration via T5 conformal prediction
Held-out val accuracy on real data > 60% (significant beat over synthetic 50%)

phases.title: Phase 5 — Architecture Modernization (Adam, regularization, conformal, CatBoost option)
phases.rationale: Reviewer 5 (industry comparison) flagged 32→16→3 MLP with SGD-momentum as 2015-era. CatBoost/LightGBM beat MLPs on tabular by 2-8 points AUC. Modernize the core learner.

units.title: Adam optimizer with bias correction (replace SGD-momentum)
exit_conditions: Replace vW1/vb1/vW2/vb2 with mW1/mb1/mW2/mb2 (first-moment) + vW1/vb1/vW2/vb2 (second-moment)
Bias correction terms applied: m_hat = m / (1 - β1^t), v_hat = v / (1 - β2^t)
Persisted in serialize() for checkpoint resumption
E2E convergence test still passes; Adam should reach the loss floor faster (fewer epochs)
Add benchmark test comparing Adam vs SGD on same synthetic dataset, assert Adam ≤ 1.2× SGD epoch-count for same final accuracy
abort_criteria: Adam doesn't outperform SGD on the synthetic dataset (suggests bug in second-moment update)
units.description: Reviewer 3 + Reviewer 5 both flagged. Adam is industry-standard for 2026.

units.title: L2 weight decay + early stopping + best-checkpoint
exit_conditions: L2 added to gradient: grad += weight_decay * param (default weight_decay = 1e-4)
Best-checkpoint: track best val_loss across epochs, restore weights at end of train()
Early stopping: patience=5 epochs without val improvement → break
Held-out validation samples passed via TrainOpts.validationSamples
abort_criteria: Early stopping always triggers at epoch ≤2 (suggests broken val_loss tracking)
units.description: Reviewers 3+4+5 all flagged. Modern training discipline.

units.title: Class-weighted cross-entropy + label smoothing
exit_conditions: Class weights computed from training-set inverse frequency
Label smoothing eps=0.05 in the cross-entropy target
On real JM Die corpus (where success ≫ failure), failure-class recall improves vs unweighted baseline
abort_criteria: Class weighting destabilizes training on synthetic (balanced) dataset
units.description: Reviewer 3 finding: failures and overrides are rare in real data. Without class weighting, the model collapses onto 'predict success'. Critical for real-corpus deployment.

units.title: T5 ConformalPredictionEngine wired around T1-02 outputs
exit_conditions: predictWithIntervals() returns {predicted_class, prediction_set: ['success', 'operator_override'], confidence: 0.95}
Conformal calibration set is the held-out 20% of the JM Die corpus
Validate: conformal coverage ≥ 95% on real-corpus held-out (Reviewer 5 industry baseline: Falkonry ships this)
abort_criteria: Conformal coverage < 90% (calibration broken)
units.description: Reviewer 5 flagged: 'Falkonry now ships conformal prediction'. PRISM has the engine but doesn't wire it. Wire it.

criteria: Adam matches or beats SGD on epoch-to-target-accuracy
Class weighting closes failure-class recall gap on real corpus
Conformal coverage ≥ 95% on held-out real data
Held-out val accuracy > 65% on real corpus (vs 60% baseline post-data ingest)

phases.title: Phase 6 — Runtime Tier Composition (T2 memory + T3 drift + T4 RL + T8 safety + T12 orchestrator wired)
phases.rationale: Reviewer 2 found 42 of 47 engines have ZERO production callers. Phases 1-5 wired Tier 1, FeedbackBus, and architecture upgrades. This phase wires the remaining tiers into the runtime pipeline — turning the library into a system.

units.title: T2 EpisodicMemory + PrioritizedReplay wired to FeedbackBus
exit_conditions: EpisodicMemory subscribes to 'outcome.recorded' — stores hot/warm/cold tiered memory
PrioritizedReplay subscribes — computes priority on |TD-error|^α + ε
NeuralLearningEngine.train() now optionally pulls from PrioritizedReplay sampler instead of full ledger
Test: assert prioritized batches over-sample high-error events (PER property)
abort_criteria: PER complexity bug: priority distribution doesn't match Schaul et al.'s expected shape
units.rollback_procedure: git checkout HEAD -- relevant engine files
units.description: Reviewer 2 finding: T2 has zero production callers despite being the FIRST tier built after Tier 1. Wire it now.

units.title: T3 DriftDetector wired to nightly cron + Stop hook alerting
exit_conditions: DriftDetector samples 24h rolling window of outcome events at midnight (cron)
If drift confidence > 0.5: emit alert → Stop hook surfaces 'Drift detected — recommend retrain' to operator
Tested via injected synthetic drift in a test fixture
abort_criteria: Drift detector flaps (frequent false-positive alerts)
units.description: Reviewer 5 flagged: 'no drift detection wired to retraining'. Wire it.

units.title: T4 RewardShaper + PolicyGradient wired to outcome events
exit_conditions: RewardShaper subscribes to 'outcome.finalized' — converts outcome → scalar reward (success +1, failure -10, override -2)
PolicyGradient consumes shaped rewards → REINFORCE-with-baseline step
Operator override events reduce policy probability of the overridden action
T4 test: 100 simulated overrides should measurably shift the policy distribution
abort_criteria: Reward hacking: policy converges to a metric loophole (e.g., always-recommend-the-most-conservative-feed)
units.description: Reviewer 1: memory feedback never reaches RL. Reviewer 2: T4 has zero production callers. Wire both.

units.title: T8 SymbolicConstraintEnforcer wraps T1-02 outputs (physics envelope hard-gate)
exit_conditions: All shop-floor-tier predictions (Ω≥0.95 per CLAUDE.md) flow through symbolic enforcer
Enforcer projects neural output onto Kienzle envelope, Taylor curve, machine-spindle-power, axis-rapid limit
Returns nearest feasible point + violation report
Wired into prism_safety:validate_physics — Reviewer 2 finding: this is the missing wire from safety dispatcher
Test: synthetic 'bad' neural prediction (feed > Sf) gets clamped to feasible region
abort_criteria: Enforcer over-clamps legitimate predictions (false-positive rate > 10%)

exit_conditions: orchestrate_full('predict-sf', context) returns: T1-02 prediction + T5 conformal interval + T8 envelope + T9 causal explanation

criteria: Connected-engine count rises from ≥15/47 (P3 exit) to ≥40/47
Tier 12 orchestrator query: <500ms p99 with all provenance fields
T8 enforcer blocks 0% legitimate / 100% bad-physics predictions on synthetic test
T4 RL has measurable policy shift after 100 override events

acceptance: Final state: T1-02 has correct backprop, no label leak, true minibatch SGD, statistically-validated convergence. Featurization includes physics + RAG features at 64+ input dim. FeedbackBus event flow connects ≥40/47 engines into a runtime graph. 24,545 JM Die programs ingested as training data. Adam + L2 + class-weighted CE + conformal prediction in production. T2/T3/T4/T8/T12 tiers all wired with subscribers. Reviewer 2's connected-engine count rises from 5/47 to ≥40/47.

JM Die corpus parsing coverage plateau below 90%; mitigation = WEDM-first MVP per Reviewer 5 Option A

T8 symbolic enforcer over-clamps; mitigation = staged rollout with operator override telemetry
